newsitem.title: GERMANY: Europe nickel use in stainless seen higher in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Europe nickel use in stainless seen higher in 1997.

text.p: European nickel consumption by the stainless steel industry in 1997 should rise along with rising stainless output, analyst Philippe Joly of French mining group Eramet said.

European stainless steel output was very tentatively forecast to rise by seven percent from an estimated 6.18 million tonnes in 1996, when it dropped by six percent, he told Reuters during a nickel and stainless industry meeting here.
But the growth rate of primary nickel usage would depend on the availability of nickel scrap, Joly said.
Last year, the European stainless industry consumed 216,000 tonnes of primary nickel, according to Eramet estimates, which Joly said were on the low side.
Nickel scrap usage relative to that or primary nickel increased by five percentage points on the year to 53 percent.
Joly said it was impossible to predict the ratio this year as it would depend on stainless steel production, stainless prices and the inherent nickel price value in scrap volumes.
Stainless steel production in the second quarter of 1997 would head for a record 1.78 million tonnes after 1.72 million in the first quarter and 1.66 million in fourth quarter 1996, he said.
European demand had improved since a destocking phase ended in fourth quarter 1996 and additional factors like speculative stockbuilding and new applications could be at play.
But analysts were sceptical the high level of output could be maintained in the second half of the year.
The stainless steel industry accounts for two thirds of global nickel use.
